findings.title: List-based sources are matched to our IPOs by NAME, which the page-identity rule does not cover
findings.detail: CORRECTED 2026-09-09: I measured zero normalisation collisions across 327 IPOs and reported it as reassuring. That reading was BACKWARDS. Zero collisions does not mean matching is safe - it means the normaliser is too weak to ever merge two rows, INCLUDING two that describe the same company. Proven live: ASSET RECONSTRUCTION COMPANY (INDIA) LIMITED normalises to "asset reconstruction company (india)" and Asset Reconstruction Co.(India) Ltd. to "asset reconstruction co (india)" - it strips Limited/Ltd/Pvt Ltd but NOT Company vs Co., so a duplicate of a mainboard IPO opening TODAY passes straight through. Two different identity failures, not one. (a) PER-IPO PAGE fetch - Chittorgarh detail via verifier_url - guarded by the F-44 page-identity rule; affects the 47 rank-2 fields (financial_data, financial_statements, peer_companies, ipo_valuation mcap/pe at cap, promoters.name). (b) LIST fetch - InvestorGain GMP (one report endpoint, data-read/331) and the Chittorgarh listing page - where a row is bound to our IPO by normalizeCompanyNameForMatching (investorgain-gmp-orchestrator-v2.ts:331-336, flag ENABLE_GMP_NAME_MATCH). The page-identity rule cannot help there because the page is correct; the ROW binding is what can be wrong. Exposure: gmp_records.gmp is the only field where a website is rank 1, and it is bound this way. Separately 24 distinct fields holding 4,825 values on prod come from the CG listing page by the same mechanism - segment 242, offeringType 241, listingDate 238, closeDate 237, openDate 236, isin 228, faceValue 226, issueSize 221, registrar 219, leadManagers 219. Needed: a stated binding rule (what counts as a match, what a near-match does, what an ambiguous match does) and a check on cross-bound rows.

findings.closed_in: §2.3.3 now SPECIFIES the de-duplication key, not just the principle: the exact word list to fold, the open-date condition that keeps a deliberately lossy key safe, and the rule that binding and de-duplication must NOT share a key because they need opposite error biases. Measured both directions on real data: before the merge the key found the one duplicate group on production that the shipped normaliser missed; after it, 329 production IPOs produce 329 distinct keys - zero false merges. Code half is build item 12.

findings.title: Per-field source priority must be configurable without a code change (owner requirement)
findings.detail: Today the order lives in field-priority-matrix.ts, so changing which source leads a field needs a PR and a deploy. Design: separate CAPABILITY (can this source serve this field at all - proven by fetching, updated by the verification job) from PRIORITY (of those that can, which we prefer - configurable). Priority is configurable WITHIN capability, never over it: no config may make CG rank 1 for pe_ratio or NSE rank 1 for a financial, because the result is a permanent NOT_PRINTED and a silent slide down the ranks. Three layers: config/field-sources.json in the repo (generated by the existing spec), a field_source_overrides table shaped on the existing field_protection_metadata for runtime change with no deploy, and the per-IPO admin protection that already exists. Four guards: overrides validated against capability and S-05 before taking effect, a 30-day default expiry so the override table cannot quietly become the real config, provenance records which config produced each value, and a nightly report of every active override by field and reason.

findings.title: fresh + OFS does not reconcile with issue_size on 6 of 9 live IPOs, and one is arithmetically impossible
findings.detail: DIAGNOSED 2026-09-09. RCA: the components come from the document and the total from a website - two sources describing one offer, under no obligation to agree. Every PASSING row took its total from the document; every FAILING row took it from a website. But the websites are RIGHT and our extraction is wrong, proven against NSE own wording: Kanohar NSE says fresh Rs 3,000mn = 300 Cr, we store 60; Glass Wall NSE says 600mn = 60 Cr, we store 260. Reconciliations are EXACT once NSE fresh + OFS is used: Kanohar 300 + 11,957,915 x 632 = 1,055.74 = stored total; Glass Wall 60 + 20,213,722 x 182 = 427.89 = stored total; Pranav implied OFS 35.43 Cr over 2,856,869 shares = Rs 124/share = its stored cap; Prasol 80+420=500; Karamtara 675+200=875. TWO DEFECTS: (1) ofs_issue is never extracted - all six - and it appears in two forms, rupees (OFS aggregating up to Rs 4,200 million) and shares (OFS of up to 20,213,722 equity shares), the share form needing multiplication by the cap; (2) fresh_issue mis-extracted on two of six, wrong in the DIGITS not the units, so no magnitude bound catches it - only the reconciliation check does. ASSET RECONSTRUCTION EXPLAINED 2026-09-09: not an impossible value - a DUPLICATE ROW. Two rows for one company (asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd with symbol ARCIL and bse_ipo_no 7950, issue_size 696.06 Cr, ofs 732.97 Cr; and asset-reconstruction-co-india-ltd with no symbol, issue_size 733.00 Cr). findings.title: No rule exists for what happens when two rows converge on one identifier
findings.detail: Owner question 2026-09-09. Measured: NO open or upcoming IPO has an ISIN (0 of 19) - the depository assigns it near listing, so the only permanently unique id arrives AFTER the row is created and published. The duplicate second Asset Reconstruction row carries no identifier at all: no symbol, no ISIN, no CIN, no BSE number. So one-row-per-unique-id is right but unenforceable at insert. Design now carries late-binding identity: create on the normalised name, re-check every time a stronger identifier arrives, MERGE automatically on a converging symbol/CIN/ISIN keeping the union of fields and both provenances, and use CIN earlier (8 of 13 upcoming have it; it exists from incorporation, unlike a symbol or ISIN). The gap was never the identifiers - we hold four - it was having no rule for convergence. WORKED EXAMPLE 2026-09-09: the Asset Reconstruction merge (F-55) is the first time this convergence was resolved by hand, and scripts/merge-duplicate-ipo.mjs is what the rule would have to automate. What it settled in practice: the survivor is the row holding the strong identifiers (symbol/CIN/BSE number), never the one with the larger field count alone; a disagreeing strong identifier REFUSES the merge because it proves two offers; columns move only where the survivor is empty; person-created rows (watchlists, clicks, reviews, audit) are repointed while scraper-derived rows are deleted; the dropped slug becomes a redirect so the URL keeps resolving; and every moved column writes a field_sources row keeping previous_source. Those six decisions are the content the missing rule needs.

findings.title: The 30/90 anchor lock-in split does not exist before 1 April 2022, but the formula is unconditional and the 22:00 job walks backwards into those IPOs
findings.detail: Appendix A.1 row 182 states: "computed: allotment_date + 30 days - SEBI ICDR 2018 Schedule XIII Part A, VERIFIED 2026-09-08 (50% locked 30 days from allotment, split rule for issues opening on or after 1 Apr 2022)", and row 183 the same for +90. §2.5.3's audit table then states the formula with no condition at all: "1-2 | `lock_in_50_percent_date`, `lock_in_remaining_date` | `allotment_date` + 30 / + 90 | **SEBI ICDR Sch. XIII Part A - verified**". The design has therefore recorded the effective date in the appendix and dropped it from the formula it will build. For any issue that opened before 1 April 2022 the SEBI (ICDR) Fourth Amendment 2021 does not apply: the whole anchor allotment was locked in for 30 days from allotment and there is NO 90-day tranche, so writing `allotment_date + 90` for those IPOs invents a lock-in expiry that never existed - on a date traders watch, which is §2.5.3's own reason for caring. §6.1 makes this reachable rather than theoretical: the 22:00 job picks "`status` is `LISTED` or `CLOSED`, and `close_date` is before today ... Ordered by `close_date` **descending**" with no lower bound, and §5.3 confirms pre-2023 rows are in that backlog ("a correct 2022 row would be rejected by a 2026 rule"). Separately, the citation itself is misquoted in the direction that matters for OD-25: §2.5.3 says "50% of an anchor's allotment is locked for 30 days from the date of allotment, the remaining 50% for 90 days", while Schedule XIII Part A as amended reads that fifty per cent of the shares allotted to anchor investors is locked in for NINETY days and the REMAINING fifty per cent for THIRTY days. The pair of dates is unaffected; the claim 'verified against the regulation' is not. findings.title: The SME lot-value check is written two different ways, and the weaker one can never fire
findings.detail: §1.2 row 4 states the check as "`lot x floor >= Rs 10,000` mainboard; `>= Rs 1,00,000` SME (2 lots x Rs 50k floor, SEBI 2025)" - i.e. ONE lot must be worth at least Rs 1,00,000. §1.11 states the same check as "the lot-value check is `2 x lot x floor >= Rs 1,00,000`" - i.e. one lot need only be worth Rs 50,000. The two differ by a factor of two and an implementer will build one of them. The second is the one that cannot work: the design's own §2.6 says "an SME lot is about Rs 1,00,000-1,50,000" (line 1594), so `2 x lot x floor >= Rs 1,00,000` is satisfied by every real SME IPO with a 2x margin and would still pass a lot priced at half the exchange floor - a check that cannot fail is not a check. The mainboard side has the mirror problem: `lot x floor >= Rs 10,000` is one-sided, so a lot size wrong by 10x upward (Rs 1,50,000 per lot on a mainboard IPO) passes, and the SEBI minimum-application band for a mainboard issue is a RANGE of roughly Rs 10,000-15,000 evaluated at the cap of the price band, not an open-ended floor evaluated at the bottom. ARCIL, open today, is the worked example: 107 x 139 = Rs 14,873 at the cap sits inside the band; the design checks 107 x 132 = Rs 14,124 at the floor against a lower bound only. [domain review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.2 row 4 vs §1.11 (SME on BSE / SME on NSE rows); design's own SME lot range at §2.6]
findings.fix_in: NOT fixed in this round. Pick one statement and put it in the validation configuration once (§5.3), not in two prose tables. Recommended: per-lot, two-sided, at the CAP - mainboard `10,000 <= lot x cap <= 15,000`; SME `1,00,000 <= lot x cap <= 2,00,000` - and express the 2-lot minimum-application rule separately as `lot_multiple = 2` (see F-63) rather than folding it into the lot-value bound, which is what made the two statements diverge.
findings.fixed_in: FIXED 2026-09-09 in the delta run. The SME lot-value check is now stated ONCE, identically in §1.2 row 4 and §1.11, as `lot_multiple × lot × floor ≥ ₹1,00,000` with lot_multiple read from the row; the mainboard check became two-sided (₹10,000–₹15,000) so a lot ten times too large also fails.

Applied without effective dates to the closed-IPO backlog, a correct 2022 row would be rejected by a 2026 rule." findings.title: The allocation check has the QIB inequality the wrong way round, allows the categories not to add up, and can double-count anchor shares
findings.detail: §1.3 field 50 states the check as: "QIB + NII + retail <= 100; book-built QIB >= 50 (>= 75 where the regulation is cited)". SEBI ICDR 2018 Regulation 32(1), for a book-built issue under Reg 6(1), reads the other way: NOT MORE THAN fifty per cent of the net offer to QIBs, NOT LESS THAN fifteen per cent to non-institutional investors, NOT LESS THAN thirty-five per cent to retail individual investors. Only the Reg 6(2) route (Reg 32(2)) makes QIB a floor at seventy-five per cent, with NII not more than fifteen and retail not more than ten. As written, `QIB >= 50` accepts a Reg 6(1) issue showing 65% QIB - a value the regulation forbids and a mis-extraction the check exists to catch - and never tests the retail 35% floor or the NII 15% floor at all, which is where a mis-parsed basis-of-allotment table actually goes wrong. `<= 100` compounds it: the three categories must exhaust the net offer, so a row summing to 70 (one category dropped in extraction) passes silently. Third, field 72 `ipo_details.anchor_shares_offered` is a separate stored field, but the anchor portion is carved OUT of the QIB portion under Schedule XIII, so any sum that adds field 72 to fields 67-69 double-counts it - and the design never says which convention the four fields use. [domain review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.3 field 50 (allocation_pct); Appendix A.1 rows 50, 67-69, 72]
findings.fix_in: NOT fixed in this round. Split the rule by route, keyed on field 54 `sebi_regulation_cited`: Reg 6(1) -> QIB <= 50, NII >= 15, retail >= 35; Reg 6(2) -> QIB >= 75, NII <= 15, retail <= 10; fixed-price -> its own split. Replace `<= 100` with `= 100 +/- 0.5` over the three net-offer categories. State in the field spec that `anchor_shares_offered` is a subset of `qib_shares_offered` and add `anchor <= qib` as its check, so the double-count cannot be introduced by the writer.
findings.fixed_in: FIXED 2026-09-09 in the delta run. §1.3 field 50 is now split by route on `sebi_regulation_cited`: Reg 6(1) QIB ≤ 50 / NII ≥ 15 / retail ≥ 35; Reg 6(2) QIB ≥ 75 / NII ≤ 15 / retail ≤ 10; categories sum to 100 ± 0.5; the anchor portion is inside the QIB share, never added on top.

findings.title: "No draft prospectus stage" is wrong for a follow-on offer, and A.2's zero-N/A count contradicts §1.11's own sentence
findings.detail: §1.11 says of FPO: "The rule is written and not exercised: no draft prospectus stage, so rank 1 is the RHP or prospectus directly; everything else follows mainboard." A further public offer is made under the same public-issue chapter of SEBI ICDR 2018 as an IPO and a draft offer document IS filed with the Board (Reg 25/26); the only FPOs that skip it are those eligible for the fast-track route (Reg 155), which is a per-issue condition, not a property of the offering type. Building the FPO plan on 'there is no draft' means the DRHP that does arrive has no document-type rank, and §6.5's warning applies directly - "A re-extraction must resolve a **real document type**, or type ranking degrades to newest-write-wins and an old draft overwrites a final price band advertisement." The same sentence also contradicts Appendix A.2, which gives "FPO | 0 | 0 | 240" - zero fields N/A. By §1.11's own claim at least field 55 `promoter_group_transactions_since_drhp` must be N/A (§1.3 says it is "only meaningful when a DRHP preceded the RHP"), and field 51 `pre_ipo_placement` is meaningless for a company already listed. A.2 already warns FPO "is the least trustworthy column in this appendix"; the warning is not a substitute for the fix. [domain review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.11 (FPO row), Appendix A.2 (FPO row), against §1.3 field 55 and §6.5]
findings.fix_in: NOT fixed in this round. Rewrite the FPO row as: the draft offer document exists unless the issue is fast-track under Reg 155, so the document-type ladder is DRHP -> RHP -> PROSPECTUS exactly as mainboard, and a missing DRHP is NOT_PRINTED rather than NOT_APPLICABLE. Mark fields 51 and 55 N/A for FPO and regenerate A.2 so its FPO column stops claiming 240/240. Add a first-FPO acceptance step to the build sequence: the first row that arrives with `offering_type = FPO` is walked by hand before its page is published.
findings.fixed_in: FIXED 2026-09-09 in the delta run, by removing the false claim rather than by keeping it: the FPO row no longer says there is no draft stage.

findings.title: The design never says which of the two Indian meanings of 'OFS' the 19 production rows are, and A.2 grants them 205 fields the exchange mechanism does not have
findings.detail: §1.11 says: "**OFS** | 19 | No fresh issue: field 35 is legitimately 0 and `issue_size = ofs_issue`. No objects of the offer (field 27 empty is correct). No DRHP stage." In Indian primary markets 'OFS' names two different things. (a) The offer-for-sale COMPONENT of a public issue - which is what field 36 `ipo_details.ofs_issue` measures, and which is a property of an IPO, not an offering type; §2.5.4 uses it in exactly that sense ("fresh Rs 600 mn + OFS 20,213,722 shares"). (b) The SEBI OFS-through-stock-exchange mechanism, by which promoters of an ALREADY LISTED company sell via a one- or two-day exchange auction: there is no offer document, no price band (a floor price only), no lot size, no anchor book, no registrar basis of allotment, no listing date, and settlement is on the exchange. The design reads as (b)-shaped in saying 'no DRHP stage' while ranking rank 1 as the document and, in Appendix A.2, granting "OFS | 19 | 35 | 205" - 205 resolvable fields including the price band, the anchor book, the lot and the allotment timetable, none of which the exchange OFS mechanism produces. A.2 itself notes "OFS and BUYBACK (20 IPOs) have never had a single provenance row written", so nothing has ever tested which reading is true. If those 19 rows are meaning (a) they are mis-typed and are IPOs; if they are meaning (b) the field plan is wrong for all 19. [domain review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.11 (OFS row), Appendix A.2 (OFS row), against §2.5.4's use of the same word and §1.3 field 36]
findings.fix_in: NOT fixed in this round. Resolve it with a probe before build item 1, not in prose: read the 19 rows' `offering_type`, `price_range_min/max`, `lot_size` and document set from production and state which meaning they carry. If they are exchange-mechanism OFS, mark the price-band, lot, anchor and allotment families N/A for the type and regenerate A.2; if they are IPOs with an OFS component, correct `offering_type` and let F-20's plan-rebuild rule pick them up. Either way, name the two meanings in the glossary so `offering_type = OFS` and `ipo_details.ofs_issue` are never read as the same fact.
findings.fixed_in: FIXED 2026-09-09 in the delta run, by MEASURING rather than by choosing. probes/ofs-rows.mjs read all 19 rows on production: 0 have a lot size, 0 have any document, 1 has a full price band, 0 have a fresh issue and 0 have ofs_issue set. They are SEBI's OFS-through-stock-exchange mechanism, not the offer-for-sale component of a public issue. §1.11's row is rewritten, and two sentences it carried are now known false: `issue_size = ofs_issue` (no row has ofs_issue) and the implied document ladder (no row has a document). The remaining question — whether the type gets its own page shape — is the owner's and is recorded as O-14.

findings.title: The 10-working-day window check is a public-issue rule applied to 8 rights issues that are legitimately open far longer
findings.detail: §1.2 row 6 states the check unconditionally: "`close >= open`; `close <= open + 10` working days". That bound is SEBI ICDR 2018 Reg 46 - a public issue's bid/offer period is at least three and at most ten working days including any extension on a price-band revision. It does not govern a rights issue, which is made under the rights-issue chapter and is customarily kept open for fifteen to thirty days; §1.11 already knows rights issues are structurally different ("No DRHP, no price band advertisement, no anchor round, no lot size in the IPO sense") but the date rule was not scoped with them in mind. There are 8 rights issues on production. Under §5.3's regime they would be rejected as failing a plausibility check that is correct for a class they are not in - the F-10 class the design says it closed, surviving in a rule whose Check cell carries no offering-type scope. §5.3 provides the escape ("the offering types and segments it applies to"); §1.2 does not use it. [domain review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.2 row 6 (close_date check), against §1.11 (Rights issue row) and §5.3]
findings.fix_in: NOT fixed in this round. Scope the rule in the validation configuration: `offering_type IN (IPO, FPO)` -> `3 <= working_days(open, close) <= 10`; `offering_type = RIGHTS` -> a calendar-days bound of roughly 7 to 30; NCD -> its own window from the prospectus. While auditing that rule, add the missing lower bound for public issues - the current check has none, so a one-day window passes.
findings.fixed_in: FIXED 2026-09-09 in the delta run. §1.2 row 6 is now scoped by offering type: IPO/FPO 3–10 working days (Reg 46), RIGHTS 7–30 calendar days, NCD its own window. The 8 rights issues on production are no longer rejected by a public-issue rule.

findings.title: A rights issue's record date and entitlement ratio are absent from the 240 fields and are not declared as a gap, unlike the equivalent NCD gap
findings.detail: §1.11 handles the rights issue purely by subtraction - "Fields 93-109, 131-137 are `NOT_APPLICABLE`, not gaps" - and adds nothing. The two facts a rights-issue reader needs above all others are the RECORD DATE (you must hold the shares on that date to receive the entitlement) and the ENTITLEMENT RATIO (for example 3 rights shares for every 5 held), plus the rights-entitlement trading window on the exchange. None of the 240 fields in Appendix A.1 carries any of them, and §1.11 does not list them as missing. The design does exactly the right thing one row above, for NCD: "Its own prospectus is rank 1 for coupon, tenor and rating - **none of which we currently store**, which is a gap this design surfaces rather than closes." The same sentence is owed to rights issues; without it, 8 production rows get a page whose most important dates are structurally unreachable and nobody is told why. [domain review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.11 (Rights issue row) vs the NCD row directly below it; Appendix A.1 (no record-date or entitlement-ratio field among the 240)]
findings.fix_in: NOT fixed in this round. Add one sentence to the Rights issue row naming record date, entitlement ratio and the RE trading window as fields we do not store, with the letter of offer as rank 1 and the exchange rights-issue circular as rank 2 - the same treatment the NCD row already gets. Then either add the three columns in build item 1 (they are cheap and the class is 8 rows) or record the decision not to, so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight.
findings.fixed_in: FIXED 2026-09-09 in the delta run. The rights-issue row now names the record date, the entitlement ratio and the rights-entitlement trading window as fields we do not store, with the letter of offer as rank 1 — the same treatment the NCD row already had.

findings.title: Item 1's Files section never rewires the actual write call sites for 3 of its 8 named tables (ipo_details, financial_statements, ipo_valuation) — they keep writing through the old, non-consolidated path
findings.detail: Item 1's Purpose and Schema sections claim all eight tables — 'ipo_details, financial_statements, ipo_valuation, ipo_risk_factors, promoters, anchor_investors, ipo_intermediaries, peer_companies' — get 'per-field priority resolution, field_sources rows, and data_conflicts detection'. But the card's Files table only names call-site changes for the five whole-row-replace tables: 'The five replaceAllowed(...) call sites for whole-row replace (promoters line 1390, promoter_acquisition_ranges line 1435, ipo_risk_factors line 1518, ipo_intermediaries line 1644, peer_companies line 1701)... are replaced by calls to orchestrator.consolidatedUpsertChildRows', plus anchor-persister.ts:540-541. It never names a change to the ipo_details, financial_statements, or ipo_valuation write sites. I read those three sites in scraper/src/services/filing-persister.ts (this session, current main): ipo_details is written via `await deps.ipoDetailsWriter.upsert(ipoId, {...detailsWritable, dataSource: source})` followed by a bare `await trackField('ipo_details', col)` per column (~line 991-996); financial_statements via `await deps.financialStatements.upsert({ipoId, fiscalYear, basis, ...})` followed by `await trackField('financial_statements', 'rows')` (~line 1250-1273); ipo_valuation via `await deps.ipoValuation.upsert({ipoId, pricingEvent, ...})` followed by `await trackField('ipo_valuation', pricingEvent)` (~line 1315-1355). `trackField` is a bare provenance stamp with no priority resolution and no conflict detection — a completely different, third write pattern from the five the card actually rewires. Item 1's own worked example even calls `consolidatedUpsertChildRows(ipoId, 'financial_statements', ...)` as if this were already wired, but no line in the Files table tells an implementer to replace the real call at filing-persister.ts's financial_statements/ipo_valuation/ipo_details sites with that call. An implementer following the Files table literally ships the schema migration and the five replace-based rewires, runs the listed unit/integration tests (which exercise the interface directly, not filing-persister.ts's real call sites), and reports done — while revenue, EBITDA, EPS, valuation multiples and every ipo_details field keep flowing through the old no-priority-resolution path. This directly recreates, for 3 of 8 tables, the exact gap §7.1 says item 1 exists to close ('208 of 240 fields have no consolidated writer at all... the pull loop would have nowhere to put 87% of what it extracts'), and starves item 5/6's field_sources-driven walk of real provenance for financial and valuation data specifically. [engineering review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/build-cards/item-01-child-table-consolidated-writer.md — 'Files' table (rows for data-consolidation-orchestrator.ts and filing-persister.ts) and the 'Worked example' under Interfaces; contradicted by scraper/src/services/filing-persister.ts:991-1005 (ipo_details), :1250-1273 (financial_statements), :1315-1355 (ipo_valuation)]

findings.title: Item 1 adds three new UNIQUE constraints to production tables with no pre-migration duplicate check or repair step
findings.detail: Item 1's Schema section requires adding brand-new unique constraints to tables that have NEVER had one: `promoters` gets `(ipoId, normalizedName)` ('The table has no unique constraint today... because the current write path deletes every row and reinserts'), `ipo_intermediaries` gets `(ipoId, role, normalizedName)` ('none exists today because the write path is whole-table replace'), and `peer_companies` gets `(ipoId, normalizedName)` ('No unique constraint today... same replace-then-insert reason as promoters'). The card's migration section shows the field_sources/data_conflicts row_key migration in full but gives no equivalent DDL, pre-flight duplicate-scan query, or repair tool for these three NEW constraints on promoters/ipo_intermediaries/peer_companies. Because these tables were written by delete-then-insert with no identity concept until now, nothing in the current or historical write path ever prevented two rows normalizing to the same key within a single replace batch (e.g. a promoter and a group-entity of the same name both parsed from one document, or a peer company listed under two share classes) — the risk is exactly the kind the card itself names as real ('a mainboard IPO commonly has 2-4 BRLMs and several syndicate members under the same role value' is given as the reason role-alone collides, i.e. real documents already produce near-duplicate name+role combinations). Running `ALTER TABLE promoters ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE (ipo_id, normalized_name)` against a table with even one existing duplicate pair fails outright and blocks the whole migration (which also carries the field_sources/data_conflicts row_key changes item 5 and item 6 depend on), with no rollback-safe path described. [engineering review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/build-cards/item-01-child-table-consolidated-writer.md — 'Schema' table rows for promoters, ipo_intermediaries, peer_companies ('Requires adding a unique constraint...')]
findings.fix_in: NOT fixed in this round. Before generating the migration, run a duplicate-scan query per table (`GROUP BY ipo_id, normalized_name HAVING count(*) > 1` for promoters/peer_companies; `GROUP BY ipo_id, role, normalized_name HAVING count(*) > 1` for ipo_intermediaries) against staging and prod, and add a repair step (keep newest by updated_at, or merge) to the card before the ADD CONSTRAINT statement — or gate the constraint addition behind a script that repairs-then-migrates in one deploy, the same pattern item 11 already uses for its own repair tool.

Order is now stated in §7.1: add and backfill the column, re-run the scan with the REAL normaliser, then add the constraint. Zero duplicate groups under a stand-in lower-and-trim normalisation today

findings.title: field_extraction_failures.rowKey is defined nullable with a 'null for singleton tables' comment, contradicting item 1's explicit non-null '' convention for the same key — breaking the join item 4's own comment promises
findings.detail: Item 1's Schema section is emphatic and specific about row_key's nullability, twice: 'Never null — a nullable column can't sit inside a unique constraint the way an empty string can (two NULLs are not equal under a unique index; two '' are), which is exactly why '' is the singleton sentinel, not null' — and defines it as `rowKey: varchar('row_key', { length: 200 }).notNull().default('')`. Item 5's ipo_field_plan repeats the identical convention verbatim for the same reason. Item 4's Schema, however, defines field_extraction_failures.rowKey as `varchar('row_key', { length: 100 })` — no `.notNull()`, no `.default('')` — with a comment reading 'Item 1's row_key (null for ipos and every singleton child table; populated for financial_statements/promoters/anchor_investors/etc. rows, matching field_sources.row_key exactly so the two tables join)'. That comment both misstates item 1's own rule (item 1 uses '' for singletons, never null) and then claims a join guarantee ('matching field_sources.row_key exactly') that the chosen nullability breaks: in SQL, `NULL = ''` evaluates to NULL/false, so a JOIN or WHERE clause correlating field_extraction_failures.rowKey with field_sources.rowKey or ipo_field_plan.rowKey on a singleton-table row (ipos, ipo_details, anchor_investors, financial_data) will never match, silently losing exactly the cross-table correlation ('which document said this failed, and what does its provenance record show') that item 4's own comment says this column exists for. The column is also declared varchar(100) here versus varchar(200) in item 1/item 5, a second, smaller inconsistency in the same field. [engineering review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/build-cards/item-04-per-field-validation.md — 'Schema' section, `fieldExtractionFailures` table, `rowKey` column and its comment; contradicted by docs/design/build-cards/item-01-child-table-consolidated-writer.md 'Schema' section's rowKey definition and rationale, and docs/design/build-cards/item-05-ipo-field-plan-table.md's identical rowKey definition]
findings.fix_in: Build card item-04 changes field_extraction_failures.row_key to NOT NULL DEFAULT '', matching items 1 and 5. NULL = '' is false in SQL, so the nullable version broke the join its own comment promised.

findings.detail: D15's stated purpose: "OD-25 makes a probe output, a saved fixture or a file:line the only acceptable basis for a rank ... it refuses an evidence reference that does not resolve to a file that exists (an unfollowable citation is an invented one, D11's lesson applied to sources)". Its entire assertion is: var p = path.join(EV_DIR, String(ref).split('#')[0]); if (fs.existsSync(p)) evHave++;  MUTATION TEST RUN: I rewrote every one of the 105 refs in docs/design/evidence.json to 'fixtures/investorgain/gmp-live.json' — a 29-key InvestorGain GMP report that contains no registrar, no face value, no EPS, no NSE/BSE/Chittorgarh data at all — and re-ran the gate. Every one of the wrong matches in F-84 through F-88 passes D15 today, and so would 105 refs pointing at a single unrelated file. The ratchet is a ratchet on path-existence, not on evidence. findings.title: The prefix rule reintroduces the exact "PAT Margin" class the mapper's own comment claims to have blocked: financial_statements.pat is evidenced by "P/E (x)"
findings.detail: The mapper's comment: "A label may not carry a token that CHANGES what the number is. 'PAT Margin' contains every token of `pat` and is a different quantity ... Evidence for the wrong quantity is the most expensive kind of wrong, because it looks right." The committed output says: financial_statements.pat | CG | how='all tokens in label' | label='P/E (x)' | fixture=chittorgarh/vinod-texworld-ltd.html | label_extras=[]. ROOT CAUSE, re-derived from the code: hasToken accepts (a.startsWith(t) && a.length - t.length <= 2). The synonym 'pat' therefore matches the one-letter label token 'p' from "P/E (x)" (3-1=2). MEANING_CHANGERS blocks 'margin' but "P/E (x)" tokenises to ['p','e','x'] and carries no blocked word, so the guard never fires. The same rule makes 'eps'~'e' and 'pbv'~'p'. This is not a lone slip; the same matcher produced four more wrong-QUANTITY pairs I checked: ipo_valuation.price_cap | CG | 'Market Cap at Offer Price' (a Rs139 price cap evidenced by Rs4,516.07 Cr market cap); ipo_demand_graph.is_cut_off | NSE | 'Cut-off time for UPI Mandate Confirmation' and the identical BSE key (a boolean bid-at-cut-off flag evidenced by a clock time); subscriptions.retail_subscription | NSE | 'Maximum Subscription Amount for Retail Investor' sample "Rs. 2,00,000" (a subscription multiple evidenced by a static regulatory cap — and the SAME label is the correct evidence for ipo_details.max_retail_subscription, so one label backs two columns that are different things); ipos.segment | NSE | 'series' sample "EQ" (MAINBOARD/SME evidenced by a trading series). SECOND MECHANISM, same matcher: MEANING_CHANGERS includes 'peer', so a label containing "peer" is REJECTED as an extra token — which makes it structurally impossible for a peer_companies.* column to be evidenced by a peer-table label, and forces every peer column onto the ISSUER's own row instead: peer_companies.eps | CG | 'EPS (Rs)', peer_companies.ronw | CG | 'RoNW', peer_companies.eps | DOC | 'eps_basic_by_fy'. The guard is one-directional and inverts its own intent for that table. [verification review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/probes/evidence-map.mjs:214-219 (hasToken), :236-247 (MEANING_CHANGERS); docs/design/probes/evidence-map.out.json (pairs for financial_statements.pat, ipo_valuation.price_cap, ipo_demand_graph.is_cut_off, subscriptions.retail_subscription, ipos.segment, peer_companies.*)]

findings.title: ipos.close_date is evidenced by the financial table's "Period Ended" header while the real "Close date" label sits in the same file
findings.detail: Committed pair: ipos.close_date | CG | label='Period Ended' | sample='31 Mar 2026 | 31 Mar 2025 | 31 Mar 2024' | fixture=chittorgarh/asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd.html. findings.title: D2 promises "no generator-owned count is hand-typed into the prose" and inspects exactly two phrase shapes — it passes on the stale numbers of F-89
findings.detail: D2's message on PASS is the unqualified sentence "No generator-owned count is hand-typed into the prose." Its complete implementation is: const handTyped = [[/the (\d+) sourced fields/g, 'plan-row count in prose'], [/\bexactly (\d+)\b(?=[^|]*E-1)/g, 'E-1 count in prose']]; — two regexes for two specific sentences. It examines nothing else. Every generator-owned number in F-89 — "114 of 386 pairs", the per-source columns 19/38, 15/40, 31/69, and "cut the total to 114" — is hand-typed into the prose, is currently WRONG, and D2 reports [PASS] D2 No generator-owned count is hand-typed into the prose. The design's stated standard of proof rests on checks like this one; a check whose PASS line asserts a general property while its body tests two string patterns is the same failure shape as D10c (which the design records as having been decoration twice). It is not that D2 does nothing — it is that its PASS line certifies far more than it looked at, and the gap is where F-89 lived undetected through a round explicitly about verification. [verification review, 2026-09-09; where: docs/design/check-design-consistency.mjs (D2, the handTyped array and its two regexes)]

findings.title: One number, 52,731,946, is the recorded evidence for four distinct columns, and the other source's evidence for the same IPO's share count is 43% smaller — nothing compares them
findings.detail: For the same IPO (ARCIL) the committed evidence records: ipo_valuation.shares_at_cap | DOC | label='total_offer_shares_at_cap' | sample='52731946'; ipo_valuation.total_shares_at_cap | DOC | 'total_offer_shares_at_cap' | '52731946'; ipo_valuation.ofs_shares | DOC | 'ofs_shares' | '52731946'; anchor_investors.total_shares_offered | DOC | 'total_offer_shares_at_cap' | '52731946'. Four columns that are four different quantities — the total offer, the OFS component, and the anchor allocation — all evidenced by the same figure. If ofs_shares == total_offer_shares_at_cap is truly what the extractor produced, then fresh issue = 0 for this IPO, which makes the design's A7 invariant ("fresh + OFS = total at the same price point", line 629) trivially satisfied and unable to detect anything on this fixture; and an anchor allocation equal to the entire offer is not possible under SEBI's anchor cap. The mapper records label and fixture per pair and never compares the VALUES two sources give for the same quantity on the same IPO, so a 43% cross-source disagreement and a physically impossible anchor figure both pass as evidence. findings.title: Seven findings filed by a parallel run were lost, because two writers shared one file

The parent session was editing the same file, and its write won: the file on disk went back to 94 findings and the seven were gone. findings.fixed_in: FIXED 2026-09-09 by restoring all seven from the run's report, and by the rule that follows: a parallel run NEVER writes a file the parent also writes. It writes its own file (`findings-<slug>.json`) and the parent merges. The same rule already applies to the design document and is why no walkthrough run edits it.

findings.title: D3 could notice a WRONG count of E-1, never a DELETED one

findings.fixed_in: D3 in docs/design/check-design-consistency.mjs: the word list covers one to twenty, and the check now asserts BOTH that the correct word is stated at least once and that no other number word appears in an E-1 phrase. findings.title: D6 was satisfied by any table quoting the words 'open and upcoming'

findings.fixed_in: D6 now finds the blockquote line beginning '> **Scope (owner, <date>):' and asserts it still names open and upcoming IPOs; its PASS line prints the sentence it found. Proven by the case 'D6 phase-1 scope - delete the owner scope statement'.

findings.title: D8 held a floor of 12 citations against a document carrying 52

findings.fixed_in: D8 is now a ratchet against the committed version, the same shape as D15: it reads HEAD of the design, and a fall in the citation count fails the gate unless the design carries a line "Citations reduced deliberately: <reason>". findings.title: D9 could not match the string it existed to forbid
findings.detail: D9's pattern was /phases*2/i — the letters 'phase', then zero or more 's', then '2'. It cannot match 'phase 2', which is the only way anybody writes it, so the check had never been capable of failing. Its declaration filter carried the mirror-image bug (it required one or two characters between 'no' and 'phase', so it did not match 'There is no phase 2' either), and only the first bug kept the gate green. Owner, 2026-09-08: 'there is no phase 2'.
findings.fixed_in: D9 matches /phase\s*2\b/i, and the filter that exempts the sentence DECLARING there is no phase 2 was corrected with it. Proven by the case 'D9 non-existent phase - park an item in "phase 2"'.

findings.title: D12's negation list was a universal excuse for putting a document read back on a clock

findings.fixed_in: D12's NEGATION now lists only words that actually deny the behaviour or place it in the past (never, not, no longer, nothing, used to, is/was removed, stops being/doing). Proven by the case 'D12 documents on a clock - re-read every 30 minutes, in a sentence containing "until"'.

findings.title: Test of the three-part identity logic on real IPOs: 2 pass, 4 fail

findings.title: The equity ISIN exists BEFORE the IPO (from the company's demat set-up), but no source we read gives it before listing
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-23 on the NSE IPO's own RHP (local copy RHP-4e566b15.pdf): p.476 and p.525 state "tripartite agreements with NSDL and CDSL dated October 11, 2007 and November 25, 2016 respectively, for dematerialisation of the Equity Shares"; p.536 states the company "may request the Depositories to suspend/ freeze the ISIN in depository system from or around the date of this Red Herring Prospectus till the listing" (per NSDL/CIR/II/28/2023 and CDSL/OPS/RTA/POLCY/2023/161, both dated August 8, 2023). This corrects the earlier working assumption (this session) that the ISIN only exists at listing. It remains true that the DRHP and RHP do not print the ISIN (0 'INE' matches in either) and neither exchange API returned it during the IPO (F-126). Web research (secondary sources; sebi.gov.in and nsdl.co.in fetches reset) says ICDR Reg 7 requires promoter shares in demat and depository agreements before filing, and that a fresh issue of the same fully-paid class uses the same ISIN (a partly-paid issue gets a separate IN9 ISIN) - UNCONFIRMED from the regulation text. A pre-listing lookup was tried: nsdl.co.in/isin_search.php and master_search_res.php returned no connection (HTTP 000) from the laptop. If a free pre-listing ISIN source is proven, the ISIN is the only identifier common to NSE, BSE and the depositories for the same shares. Related: F-124, F-126. Open for owner decision.

findings.title: The free exchange quote endpoints return a post-listing price, but NSE needs the newer API and the exact trading series
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 00:5x-07:2x IST with Node fetch from the laptop. BSE getScripHeaderData (api.bseindia.com/BseIndiaAPI/api/getScripHeaderData/w?scripcode=N) returns 200 without cookies: Hero Motors 544936 LTP 98.51 (IssueChgVal +14.51); NSE IPO 544937 returns 200 with LTP "-" (not trading yet). NSE /api/quote-equity returns 403 Access Denied even after the session warm-up that makes /api/all-upcoming-issues return 200, so the old endpoint is unusable. NSE /api/NextApi/apiClient/GetQuoteApi?functionName=getSymbolData&marketType=N&series=S&symbol=X returns 200 with that same session: HEROMOTORS series EQ lastPrice 98.4, listingDate 23-Sep-2026, boardStatus Main; ICELCO series SM lastPrice 134.5, listing 10-Jul-2026, SME; VINOD series ST lastPrice 72.85, listing 17-Sep-2026, SME, lastUpdateTime 23-Sep-2026 16:00:00. A wrong series gives 404 (VINOD EQ, VINOD SZ, ICELCO EQ) or an empty body (ICELCO ST). So SME trading series differ between stocks (SM vs ST), and the post-listing price job must use the stock's real trading series (or try EQ, BE, SM, ST and keep the one that answers) and must treat 404 as "wrong series or no such symbol", not as delisting evidence by itself (section 2.3.3.x delisting counts three consecutive no-such-symbol answers). The NSE response carries its own lastUpdateTime, which is the as-of time the page label needs. Related: OD-29, OD-54.

findings.title: A data-job slot never closes: the document retry timer makes the same documents due on every wake
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 08:4x IST by a read-only read of /var/log/ipodhan-scraper-wake-staging.log on staging release 084928e0 (contains #935, not #941). The 00:00 IST data-job slot started at 00:15 and logged 'data job slot 00:00 IST incomplete: pass=discovery,listed_deferred - continuing next wake' on all 16 wakes 00:15-07:45 and never 'complete'; the 08:15 wake opened the 08:00 slot with the same two passes incomplete. 'discovery' there is the document cycle's own finding pass (document-cycle.ts:524 budgetExhausted): true on all 16 wakes while found was 0-2 and blocked 5-74 per wake (29-127 network calls per wake). The mechanism (established from code at 084928e0): the document state machine makes every open document due again on a timer - RETRY_MINUTES NOT_YET_FILED 30, BLOCKED_FRESH 30, NOT_FOUND 60 (document-state-machine.ts:465-477) - while wakes are 30 minutes apart and the discovery pass has a 60-second budget (CYCLE_BUDGET.DISCOVERY_MS, :774). So every continuation wake finds the same open documents due again and runs out of budget (00:45 wake: 33 of 59 candidates reached in 69 s, 124 network calls). Blocked documents ARE re-tried every wake: the per-wake blocked counter counts every BLOCKED_ALL outcome (document-discovery-runner.ts:2418), but the 'Document BLOCKED_ALL' log line fires only on first entry (document-state-machine.ts:656, 'P2 once on entry, not every cycle') - the 00:45 wake had blocked 74 and 6 log lines. listedDeferred does not converge because a LISTED IPO counts complete only when nothing is due (document-cycle.ts:961), and the timer keeps making rows due. The timer is exactly what §2.1 and OD-21 already remove ('The timed backoff retry is removed ... not true today'). listedDeferred went 6,4,2,4,2 with listedCap 2 - not converging. Effect: the document job ran every 30 minutes all night (about 1,000 network calls) instead of once per OD-19 slot. The non-slot skip works (22:15-23:45 wakes skipped the document cycle; the 14:00 slot closed at 21:45). Same class as #943 (due-step discovery stamp), second mechanism. Related: F-142, OD-19, OD-55.

findings.title: Structural field-lookup failures default to TRANSIENT and get a timed backoff retry
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 from the staging wake log (00:45 IST wake, release 084928e0) and code: 340 'PASS 3: every rank failed for this field, at least one TRANSIENT' lines for 320 distinct (IPO, field) pairs, whose 622 failure reasons are all structural (NO_MAPPING 320, NO_DOCUMENT_PROVENANCE 265, 37 other). A fetcher that does not set transient=false is treated as transient (field-plan-walk.ts ~788, answer.transient !== false), and recordOutcome then writes a doubling backoff 15 min to 6 h (ipo-field-plan-repository.ts:106-107). That is a timed retry, which OD-21 ('no timed retry') and §2.5 ('never on a backoff timer') forbid; a structural gap should be recorded as definitive. Not proven: that the same pairs are re-asked on every wake (one wake's log only). Related: F-151, #943.

findings.title: Real exchange filings are encrypted with an owner password only; a blank-password open succeeds
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 on the laptop (read-only, no network): of 45 locally saved offer-related PDFs (pdf-parser-test/drhps, IPODhan-backups), 3 carry /Encrypt, and all 3 are copies of one real BSE anchor allocation report (ANCHOR_ALLOCATION_REPORT-4e5a4f9d.pdf, sha256 4e5a4f9de9ef11f3..., dated August 27, 2026, 4 pages). Its security handler is /Filter /Standard, /V 4, /R 4, /P 2820, /EncryptMetadata true: an owner (permissions) password with an EMPTY user password. pdfplumber opens it with no password argument (4 pages, text reads) and pypdfium2 opens it with password="" (4 pages). So the blank attempt of section 2.2.1 already happens implicitly for this real case, and no JS dependency (pdf-lib) is needed: the extractor is Python and both of its libraries handle it. Not measured: a real filing with a non-empty USER password (the case where the blank attempt fails and the document must be marked unreadable with its cause); none exists in the local sample. findings.title: An NSE offer-document zip holds several distinct documents, and all but one are thrown away
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 by reading the zip index (HTTP Range request on the central directory, no full download) of all 41 distinct RHP/DRHP/PROSPECTUS zip URLs in ipodhan_staging.documents: 41 of 41 hold two or more PDFs (36 hold 2, 1 holds 3, 1 holds 4, 3 hold 5). 40 carry a General Information Document (GID) beside the offer document; 5 also carry a corrigendum or a newspaper price-band / corrigendum notice: RHP_HTEL (3 corrigendum newspaper pages), RHP_ABH (3 newspaper pages), RHP_MADHURKNIT (2 corrigenda + a price-band ad), RHP_MOMSBELIEF (2 Rays of Belief corrigenda), RHP_SKYWAYS (1 corrigendum). None of the 41 is a Volume I / Volume II split, so the section 2.2.1 multi-part case in practice is distinct documents in one zip, not volumes of one. selectZipMemberForType (document-download-verifier.ts:260) keeps ONE member (the name-matched RHP, else the largest) and drops the rest. Effect on staging: of the 5 IPOs, 4 (hy-tech-engineers-ltd, abh-healthcare-ltd, madhur-knit-crafts-ltd, rays-of-belief-ltd) have NO CORRIGENDUM or PRICE_BAND_AD document at all; only skyways-air-services-ltd has one, fetched separately from the company website. So OD-30 (a corrigendum overrides the RHP for the fields it names) can never apply to a corrigendum that arrives only inside the exchange zip. Staging-wide there are 2 CORRIGENDUM documents out of 347.

findings.title: A column unit is defined four times and the definitions disagree: the manifest and the admin form say crore for five columns stored in rupees
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24. OD-67 (2026-09-21) withdrew the crore conversion: ipos.issue_size, ipo_details.fresh_issue, ipo_details.ofs_issue, ipo_valuation.mcap_at_floor and mcap_at_cap stay numeric(18,2) RUPEES. But (1) scraper/config/field-manifest.json on origin/main tags all five unit=crore (generated by scripts/generate-field-manifest.mjs from the amount-columns probe CLASS, not from the unit stored today), and tags the 7 financial_statements columns crore although section 5.2 says they carry a per-row unit column; (2) web/lib/admin/field-labels.ts labels Issue Size ₹ Crores with placeholder e.g. 5000; (3) web/lib/admin/dynamic-validation-rules.ts:174-199 validates issueSize as crore (warn below 10, warn above 100000). The admin edit page (web/app/admin/edit/[slug]/page.tsx) saves issueSize as typed, with no conversion. On ipodhan_staging 336 of 337 non-null issue_size values exceed 100000, so the ₹1 lakh crore warning fires on essentially every admin edit, and an admin who follows the label (typing 875 for Rs 875 cr) would store Rs 875. Real ADMIN values on staging are rupee-shaped (7329740494.00, 8750000000.00), so admins have typed rupees despite the label. No runtime code reads the manifest unit today (only the generator writes it), so no stored value was scaled wrongly by it. Of the five OD-48 retail rupee columns, 3 carry unit=rupee in the manifest; gmp_records.kostak_rate and subject_rate are not in the manifest at all. Second occurrence of failure class threshold-in-one-unit-column-in-another (first: item 11 scoring, 2026-09-21). Related: OD-48, OD-67, section 5.2, item 11. CORRECTION 2026-09-24 (Tier A review of PR #964): the admin claims above are overstated. The only admin screen that writes these columns is web/app/admin/dynamic/[table]/[id]/page.tsx; its API (GET /api/admin/dynamic/ipos/[id], route.ts:108-115) returns snake_case keys (issue_size) and its form reads by column name, while the Rs Crores label and the crore validator are keyed camelCase issueSize, so neither ever applies on that page. web/app/admin/edit/[slug]/page.tsx has no input that writes issue size (it only lists issueSize in protect/refresh checkboxes). So the warning does NOT fire on admin edits and no admin has been shown a crore label for this column; the live admin path shows and saves raw rupees, consistent with the real ADMIN values. The crore label/validator are dead code keyed to a shape the page never receives: a latent defect, not a live one. The manifest tag mismatch stands as measured.

findings.title: BLOCKED_ALL mostly records sources that ANSWERED without the document, not an outage; the retry timer spent 26,534 attempts on them
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 ~10:5x IST on ipodhan_staging (read-only): 448 document_fetch_state rows in BLOCKED_ALL carry 26,534 attempts in total (LISTED alone: 202 rows across 52 IPOs, attempts up to 77 each, blocked since 2026-09-04; by type BASIS_OF_ALLOTMENT_AD 52, PROSPECTUS 42, PRICE_BAND_AD 35, RATIOS_BASIS_ISSUE_PRICE 21, ANCHOR_ALLOCATION_REPORT 20, DRHP 16, RHP 16). Their last_attempt logs are mostly source ANSWERS: listing_rows POST/GET 200 (3,211 entries), untried_exchange_links/links:0 with HTTP 200 (629), no_symbol (148), not_on_board (125), HTTP 404 (106), and rung summaries such as EXCHANGES:no_link -> SEBI/COMPANY skipped. So the state name reads as "every source failed" while the sources mostly replied that they hold no such link; a true transport outage (timeout, 5xx, a 403 block) is the minority. Consequences: (1) the one post-listing attempt of PR #957 is correct for this population; (2) OD-62 already separates SOURCE_UNREACHABLE (no answer) from an answer, so an attempt where no source answered at all should not use up that one attempt. Related: F-151, F-152, OD-62, #957.

findings.title: A corrigendum is ranked above the RHP but no extractor reads it, so OD-30 can never apply
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24. scraper/src/config/document-admission-status.ts AUTO_PERSIST_DOC_TYPES (the single list both the admission stamp and the extractor dispatch read) is PRICE_BAND_AD, RHP, DRHP, PROSPECTUS, ANCHOR_ALLOCATION_REPORT; CORRIGENDUM and ADDENDUM are absent, so a stored corrigendum is admitted NOT_EXTRACTABLE and nothing reads its fields. The field-priority matrix already ranks CORRIGENDUM above RHP (field-priority-matrix.ts ~840-846, CORRIGENDUM: 0) and section 2.5.5 / OD-30 says a corrigendum overrides the RHP for the fields it names and freezes them, so the rule has an input type no code can ever produce. On ipodhan_staging: skyways-air-services-ltd CORRIGENDUM (Corrigendum-of-RHP-Skyways.pdf) is NOT_EXTRACTABLE; staging holds 2 CORRIGENDUM and 1 ADDENDUM documents in total. PR #969 (item 22) now stores the corrigenda bundled inside NSE zips (F-154: HTEL, ABH, MADHURKNIT, MOMSBELIEF, SKYWAYS), which raises the count of stored-but-unread corrigenda. Related: F-154, OD-30, item 22, item 9 ("a genuinely new corrigendum must still be fetched and read").

findings.title: 121 of 129 recently listed IPOs have no ISIN; the pull walk mostly never asks for it, and its NSE fetcher answers not-available for stocks already trading
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 on ipodhan_staging (read-only): 121 of 129 LISTED IPOs with a listing date in the last 90 days have ipos.isin NULL. The manifest ranks ipos.isin DOC -> NSE -> BSE (scraper/config/field-manifest.json), so NSE is an allowed ISIN source. For those IPOs only 34 isin plan rows exist (so most were never planned for isin), and of those: 17 NOT_AVAILABLE_YET with cause rank2:NSE:NOT_AVAILABLE_YET, 10 rank1:DOC:NOT_AVAILABLE_YET, 5 CHECK_FAILED, 1 COVERAGE_GAP (Chittorgarh has no mapping). A stock that is already trading has an ISIN, so the NSE fetcher is reading an endpoint that does not carry it after listing, while NSE GetQuoteApi getSymbolData (F-150) returns the ISIN for a listed stock. Effect: item 7 S5 (post-listing price) cannot resolve BSE scrip codes (F-155 needs the ISIN) or count delisting safely for 121 of 129 IPOs. The right fix is in the pull walk (item 6), under the normal ranks, not a side-write from the price job. Related: F-150, F-155, OD-85, item 6, item 7 S5.

findings.title: An abridged prospectus inside an NSE FORMS zip types as PROSPECTUS by its member name
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 on ipodhan_staging, read-only dry run of the item 22 stored-zip expansion (DocumentDiscoveryRunner.expandStoredZip, apply off): clay-craft-india-ltd FORMS_CLAYCRAFT.zip (https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/ipo/FORMS_CLAYCRAFT.zip) holds 'FORMS_CLAYCRAFT/Abridged Prospectus.pdf' (part 1, 437943 bytes), which classifyZipMemberName typed as PROSPECTUS, so the expansion would have stored it as a PROSPECTUS row and the next cycle would close the PROSPECTUS type FOUND on a summary. An abridged prospectus is never the offer document (the SEBI rung already refuses it, sebi-source.ts). Fixed in PR #969 round 3: classifyZipMemberName returns null (unclassified, logged, not stored) for a member whose base name says abridged; test 'never types an ABRIDGED prospectus as the Prospectus' is red without the guard. Other FORMS zips measured the same day (FORMS_TURTLEMINT) hold only forms, both unclassified.

findings.title: The pull walk supplies 1.3% of its plan: the DOC fetcher answers not-available-yet even for IPOs whose offer document is extracted
findings.detail: Rated MAJOR in this design-findings list because it is an implementation defect (the design of 2.4 is unaffected), not a design gap; its operational impact on item 6 is critical. Measured 2026-09-24 ~14:3x IST on ipodhan_staging (release f5e213e8, read-only): of 17,491 ipo_field_plan rows only 236 are SUPPLIED (1.3%); 8,623 NOT_AVAILABLE_YET, 8,406 CHECK_FAILED, 66 EXHAUSTED. By table, financial_data 0/2,639, ipo_valuation 0/1,365, financial_statements 0/1,187, subscriptions 0/823, peer_companies 0/819, ipo_intermediaries 0/637, ipo_details 155/4,195, ipos 81/2,127. The largest cause is rank1:DOC:NOT_AVAILABLE_YET (reason NOT_PUBLISHED_YET): 7,866 rows over 68 IPOs. Of those 68 IPOs, 45 have no COMPLETED RHP/DRHP/PROSPECTUS (so the answer is truthful and the gap is upstream in document fetch/extraction), but 23 DO have a COMPLETED offer document and still get DOC NOT_AVAILABLE_YET on 984 rows, e.g. axiom-gas-engineering-ltd ipos.issue_size (RHP COMPLETED 2026-09-17, last asked 2026-09-24 08:50 UTC), vama-wovenfab-ltd ipos.issue_size (RHP COMPLETED 2026-09-23), shah-investor-s-home-ltd ipos.offering_type, a-one-steels-india-ltd ipos.segment (DRHP + RHP COMPLETED). An RHP always prints its issue size, so the DOC fetcher is not reading what the extraction produced. Other causes: 344 NO_DOCUMENT_TYPE (manifest gap), plus per-source NO_MAPPING rows (Chittorgarh 45-87 per field). Related: item 6 (pull walk), F-160 (ISIN), F-152, #762, #884. RCA 2026-09-24 (item 6 PR, read-only staging proof with the real buildDocFetcher via scraper/scripts/probe-doc-fetcher.ts): 980 of the 984 rows are fields whose manifest documentType is PRICE_BAND_AD, and the fetcher's family for PRICE_BAND_AD held only PRICE_BAND_AD, contradicting section 1 (DOC = best available type; PRICE_BAND_AD > RHP > PROSPECTUS > DRHP). SME IPOs have no price-band ad, so an extracted RHP could never answer; the other 4 are ipos.symbol rows asked seconds after extraction and SUPPLIED by a lower rank. Not a key mismatch (camelCase lookup is correct) and not the store. After the fix the same 984 rows answer SUPPLIED 99 (was 39), NO_DOCUMENT_PROVENANCE 873, COLUMN_READ_NOT_IMPLEMENTED 12, NOT_AVAILABLE_YET 0. CORRECTION to this entry: 'An RHP always prints its issue size' is false on real data - axiom-gas-engineering-ltd's RHP (document 7328a5e2, page 2) prints 'AGGREGATING UP TO Rs [.] LAKHS' because the price band is not fixed at RHP filing, so DOC honestly has no rupee issue size for it until a price-band ad or prospectus. The 873 remainder are fields the filing persister never wrote a DOC provenance row for (extraction coverage, item 13), not this fetcher. Detection: nightly floor check pull_doc_nay_with_offer_doc.

findings.title: Real corrigenda are free-form notices; only 1 of 3 real ones changes a field a document may write, so OD-30 automatic override has almost nothing to act on
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 (read-only, laptop; RapidOCR available, Tesseract not). Rays of Belief: the NSE intimation letter (text layer, 3 pages) and a newspaper page (garbled font, OCR confidence 0.73-0.77) both say the Designated Stock Exchange across the RHP should be read as NSE instead of BSE -> field designated_exchange, document-owned (section 1 row 48), writable. Skyways (OCR only, conf 0.76-0.78): the Issue/Offer close date is updated from Wednesday, August 26, 2026 to Thursday, August 27, 2026 -> close_date is exchange-owned (E-1: the document is NOT a verification source) and section 2.2.1 says an OCR-only value never wins against a text page, so the spec forbids this write. Hy-Tech Engineers (HTEL, 3 newspaper pages, OCR clean): changes the Maximum Bid row of the offer-structure table on RHP page 340, prose with [●] placeholders, mapping to no stored field. Three corrigenda, three unrelated phrasings: a deterministic rule per phrasing would be fitted to the samples. The freeze OD-30 requires has no mechanism (no frozen_by_document_id column); DOCUMENT_TYPE_RANK CORRIGENDUM:0 protects ipo_details only when ENABLE_CHILD_TABLE_CONSOLIDATION is on (read in code, not run) and ranks a corrigendum above a later prospectus, contrary to section 2.5.5 rule 3. Related: F-154, F-158, OD-30, item 9, item 22. Open for owner decision.

findings.title: 8 of 129 in-window LISTED rows carry an ISIN, so BSE can be asked for few of them; NSE getSymbolData returns the ISIN; refusals arrive as HTTP 200 HTML
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 12:1x IST (item 7 S5 core proof, laptop, read-only). ipodhan_staging: of 129 LISTED rows with listing_date in the last 90 IST days, 8 carry an isin (MAINBOARD 4/58, SME 4/70), 116 carry a symbol, 0 a bse_scrip_code. NSE GetQuoteApi getSymbolData returns metaData.isinCode (HEROMOTORS INE012G01022, VINOD INE1A5U01014, CSM INE0ZK601013) and lastUpdateTime in IST (24-Sep-2026 12:17:31 = 06:47:31Z). BSE ListofScripData segment=Equity status=Active returned 5,047 rows including SME groups M (394) and MT (139), and getScripHeaderData answered for an M-group scrip (Shanti Guru 534708, 8.80, As on 22 Sep 26 | 16:00). BSE Header.LTP (117.43) and CurrRate.LTP (117.47) differed inside one Hero Motors answer. A bare User-Agent got HTTP 200 with a 14 KB HTML page from getScripHeaderData (not the Access Denied page F-155 recorded), so a refusal must be detected as a non-JSON body, never read as an answer. A non-existent NSE symbol is a 404 on all four series (EQ, BE, SM, ST). Consequence in the S5 job: a run where BSE cannot be asked (no ISIN, so no scrip code) is UNKNOWN on the BSE side and does not count toward the three no-such-symbol runs of 2.3.3.3. The ISIN gap itself belongs to the pull walk (item 6): see F-160. Related: F-150, F-155, F-160, OD-29, OD-38, item 7 S5.

findings.title: Document supersession (§2.5) is still unwired: a later, higher-precedence document does not reopen the plan rows chosen from the older one; 3 SUPPLIED rows on staging sit on an RHP after the PROSPECTUS was extracted
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-24 ~18:3x IST, read-only on ipodhan_staging (laptop, sanctioned tunnel). ipo_field_plan has chosen_document_id / chosen_document_type / chosen_sha256 but no superseded_by column, and decideSupersession (scraper/src/services/document-state-machine.ts:731) has no non-test caller on origin/main (git grep over scraper/src and packages/shared/src). Of 210 SUPPLIED plan rows with a chosen document (PRICE_BAND_AD 184, RHP 26), 3 are chosen from an RHP while a PROSPECTUS for the same IPO is extraction_status COMPLETED and was stored after the plan row last changed: jindal-supreme-india-ltd (RHP filed 2026-09-07, prospectus stored 2026-09-21 16:16 UTC), glass-wall-systems-india-ltd (RHP 2026-09-01, prospectus 2026-09-22 15:47 UTC), lcc-projects-ltd (RHP 2026-09-03, prospectus 2026-09-18 16:09 UTC); all three are ipos.company_description, plan rows last updated 2026-09-17. None of the three prospectuses carries a filing_date, and 48 of 345 documents carry one, so the spec ordering (a newer filing_date of the same type, or a higher-precedence type) cannot be evaluated for most documents even once wired. The three measured rows are low-stakes (a description), but the mechanism is the one §2.5 calls its worst error: an early figure kept for the life of the IPO. Consequence for item 10: PULL-FROZEN (pull_frozen) cannot be built as specified, since nothing records supersession; a type-rank-only reading would flag these 3 today. Not changed by OD-65: a later PROSPECTUS is a new document, not a re-read of the same one (item 9 ledger row). Related: §2.5, §2.5.1 trigger 3, item 6, item 10, item 17 (filing_date backfill). CORRECTED 2026-09-24 (item 6 core proof, scraper/scripts/repair-superseded-plan-rows.ts dry run, read-only on ipodhan_staging): the class is 28 SUPPLIED rows on the same 3 IPOs, not 3 — 20 ipo_details rows chosen from a PRICE_BAND_AD and 8 ipos rows (the 3 company_description rows from an RHP plus 5 from a PRICE_BAND_AD), each outranked by that IPO's COMPLETED PROSPECTUS within the field's document family; 0 unordered. Why a reopen alone does not let the newer document win: the walk's DOC fetcher takes the chosen document from field_sources.data_lineage.documentId (20 of the 28 point at the PRICE_BAND_AD) or, with no lineage (the 8 ipos rows), from the first COMPLETED document in family order (RHP family = RHP, DRHP, PROSPECTUS). Core gap for the amended design (answer from the document that prints the field): no per-document extraction output is persisted — extraction_logs has 0 rows on staging and no document_id column, and no scraper/src writer; document_pages stores page text only; field_sources keeps one row per field (the last writer). So 'does document X print field Y' cannot be read from the database today.

findings.title: The per-value OCR mark is dropped before consolidation: 380 offer-document values on 54 IPOs came from OCR-route documents and none says which were read off an OCR page
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-25 ~00:3x IST, read-only on ipodhan_staging. The extractor marks each field it read off an OCR'd page (scraper/scripts/ocr_pages.py annotate_fields: source_text 'OCR', ocr_confidence), but the persister's ExtractedField type (scraper/src/services/filing-persister.ts) carried only value/page/check, provenance was one lineage per document with confidence hard-coded 100, and document_field_receipts had no such column. findings.title: The per-source store is empty: no field has ever recorded what more than one source said
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-25, read-only via the sanctioned tunnel. ipodhan_staging: field_sources 13,624 rows (6,928 on table ipos); rows with witnesses not null = 0; rows with a non-empty witnesses array = 0; source='ADMIN' rows = 79. findings.title: NSE never answers 'no such symbol' for a delisted stock; it answers secStatus 'Permanent Suspended'. The no-such-symbol 404 is what a wrong series, a never-existed symbol and a RENAMED symbol return (open for owner decision: OD-38 counts no-such-symbol reads)
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-26 from the laptop, NSE GetQuoteApi getSymbolData and BSE getScripHeaderData, bodies in scraper/tests/fixtures/post-listing-price/delisting-read-shapes-2026-09-26.json. Delisted companies HDFC, IDFC, CAIRN, ESSAROIL, HEXAWARE: HTTP 200 in series EQ, secInfo.secStatus 'Permanent Suspended', isSuspended 'Suspended', lastPrice 0, lastUpdateTime null, metaData.isinCode present (HDFC INE001A01036). Temporarily suspended BALLARPUR and JETAIRWAYS: 200 in series BZ with secStatus 'Temporary Suspended', and an all-null quote row in EQ. HTTP 404 body {"error":"Unexpected end of JSON input"} is byte-identical for HEROMOTORS in the wrong series SM, for ZZNOSUCHSYM (never existed) and for ADANITRANS EQ, the old symbol of Adani Energy Solutions which still trades as ADANIENSOL. BSE: HDFC 500010 answers Category '' and Header.DisplayText 'Delisted' (not Category 'Delisted' as the #972 reader assumed), last LTP 2729.95 as of 12 Jul 23; 999999 answers Cmpname.FullN null. Consequence: a body match cannot tell a wrong series from a missing symbol; counting all-series-404 reads toward DELISTED would delist a renamed company and would never catch a delisted one. #983 therefore counts only explicit delisting reports (secStatus 'Permanent Suspended', BSE DisplayText/Category 'Delisted') and records all-series-404 as NO_SUCH_SYMBOL without counting it. OD-38's text ('three consecutive no-such-symbol reads') is open for owner decision. Related: OD-38, section 2.3.3.3, F-150, F-160, F-162, #972, #983.

findings.title: drizzle-kit 0.31.7 picks the base snapshot for `db:generate` by sorting `meta/` file names, not by the `prevId` chain, so two naming schemes in one repo make it read the chain from the wrong end
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-26 (#886, PR #1203, fix/886-snapshot-chain). `web/drizzle/migrations/meta/` mixes timestamp-named snapshots (idx 33-49, `20260906090638_`..`20260918211158_`) with sequence-named ones (idx 50-65, `0050_`..`0065_`), from a mid-history naming-scheme change. drizzle-kit's `prepareOutFolder` (`bin.cjs` 8104-8105, 21584) sorts `readdir` and takes the LAST name; `0050_..0065_` sort before every `2026..._`, so `db:generate` picked `20260918211158_snapshot.json` (id d0938915) as the base although the real `prevId` chain head is `0065_snapshot.json` (id 9472c00a). A dry `db:generate` with no schema change emitted 8,113 bytes of spurious DDL (4 CREATE TYPE, 5 CREATE TABLE, 14 ADD COLUMN, 9 ADD CONSTRAINT, 8 CREATE INDEX) re-creating everything 0050-0065 already added; applying it anywhere those migrations already ran would fail on `CREATE TYPE ... already exists`. The existing `prevId` chain-continuity check passed throughout, because the chain itself was never broken -- only the tool's SELECTION of the chain head was wrong. Fixed by a bridge snapshot (`20260926161247_snapshot.json`) whose name sorts last; detection upgraded with a new `head-sorts-last` rule in `scripts/ci/check-migration-snapshot-chain.mjs`. No owning section in `docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md` -- this is a migration-tooling defect, not a data-sourcing rule; recorded here per the findings registry rather than the spec. Failure class: `generator-base-chosen-by-name-sort-not-by-lineage` (already registered).

findings.title: NSE answers HTTP 200 with an empty `issueInfo: {}` for an issue it does not carry; that empty-but-200 reply was recorded as an answer for an SME-on-BSE issue and as a failure when every consulted exchange only abstained
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-26 (#632, PR #1200, fix/632-blocked-all), staging read-only through the tunnel: 482 BLOCKED_ALL rows on 108 IPOs. Group A: 211 rows / 62 IPOs 'settled' by exchanges, 181 rows / 44 SME IPOs by NSE:ok alone; a live GET of those 44 NSE ipo-detail?series=SME URLs returned 29 of 44 with `issueInfo: {}` (no `dataList`) -- e.g. PESHWA, ROBOKIDZ, FXML -- which had been recorded `ok`, so SEBI/company-site/verifier rungs were skipped (`exchanges_settled_it`) although NSE does not actually list those SME issues. Group B: 212 rows 'EXCHANGES:failed', of which 159 (27 IPOs) had ONLY abstentions (122 NSE:no_symbol, 37 BSE:not_on_board+NSE:no_symbol) -- nothing failed, every consulted exchange had simply abstained (OD-60), yet the verdict logic required at least one `ok` reply to avoid a failure state, so these rows went BLOCKED_ALL (P2) on their first concluded chain. Fix: NSE empty `issueInfo` now outcomes `not_carried`; `EXCHANGE_ABSTAIN_OUTCOMES` (`not_on_board`, `no_symbol`, `not_carried`) count as answered-without-link, never as coverage; exchange coverage additionally requires at least one exchange `ok`. Spec basis: OD-60 ("a source that returns zero, null or an empty value has ABSTAINED; it has not voted"), section 2.5.1. Failure class: `exchange-abstention-read-as-answer-or-failure` (already registered).

findings.title: SME document discovery asked NSE only and never consulted BSE, although the spec's stated SME order is NSE then BSE, so a BSE-only-listed SME IPO had no exchange document source at all; fixed in #1201, the SME path now asks BSE second

findings.title: the schema-drift audit only ever compared schema.ts to the live DB in one direction (declared -> live); 38 live indexes and unique constraints hand-applied to staging and never declared in schema.ts were invisible to it
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-26 (#665, PR #1204, closes #665). `assert-schema-drift.ts`'s `checkIndexes()`/`checkUniqueConstraints()` only checked schema.ts-declared objects against the live database; an object present live but never declared (e.g. staging's `ipos_symbol_key`, found 2026-09-16 by lane C while fixing the duplicate-IPO merge tool) was invisible, so the next `drizzle-kit generate` could silently attempt to drop it. Fix adds the reverse direction (`diffUndeclaredIndexes()`/`diffUndeclaredUniqueConstraints()`), matching a declared `.unique()` to its live backing object by (table, column) identity rather than by name, because Postgres's own default naming (`_key` suffix) and drizzle's default naming (`_unique` suffix) both occur live on the same schema depending on how the original migration was hand-written -- measured on staging: `admin_settings`, `ipo_details`, `ipo_financials`, `ipo_slug_redirects` all declare `.unique()` but carry `_key`-suffixed live constraints, which a name-only match would have false-positived on all four. No owning section in `docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md` -- this is a schema-tooling defect, not a data-sourcing rule. Added failure class `schema-drift-audit-checked-declared-to-live-only-not-the-reverse` (status: guarded, PR #1204 landed the fix).

findings.title: RapidOCR's page-image-sized memory allocation fails under the extractor's RLIMIT_AS ceiling and re-raises as a generic ONNXRuntimeError, so a page-size OOM was misclassified as a content failure and blocked the whole document on every retry
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-25/26 (#1046, PR #1195, refs #1046, Tier A). RapidOCR's text detector runs at the page image's full size (`limit_type: min`), so memory grows with page area; under the extractor's `RLIMIT_AS` ceiling (3072 MB, `memory_guard`) a large scanned page cannot allocate inside onnxruntime, which re-raises the allocation failure as `ONNXRuntimeError 'inference failed'` -- the underlying `bad allocation` text survived only on `__cause__`, which the memory classifier did not walk, so the extractor exited 1 (content failure) instead of exit 3 (the ceiling's own exit code). One failing page then failed the whole document on every retry. Staging had 4 HARD_FAILURE rows sharing this exact stack: kanohar-electricals-ltd PROSPECTUS (6 retries), elevate-campuses-ltd RHP (8), swastika-infra-ltd DRHP (8), runwal-enterprises-ltd PRICE_BAND_AD (4). Class covers every OCR'd page whose detector run cannot allocate under the ceiling, across all three `ocr_pages` callers (the extractor, anchor reports, corrigendum pages). Fix: `memory_guard.is_memory_exhaustion` now walks the `__cause__`/`__context__` chain; `ocr_pages.read_page_with_fallback` re-renders a failing page at progressively smaller long-edge sizes (2400px, then 1600px) before giving up. No owning section in `docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md` -- an extraction-infrastructure defect, not a sourcing/priority rule. Added failure class `ocr-page-oom-under-rlimit-misclassified-as-content-failure` (status: guarded).

findings.title: the 10-attempt block marker overwrote extraction_error with a bare terminal string, erasing whether a document was blocked by its own content or by a transient environment failure (spawn timeout, resource exhaustion) -- 4 of 6 blocked staging rows had no recoverable cause
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-26 (#583, recurrence of #396; PR #1190, round 2, Tier A). Six documents on staging carried `blocked_after_10_attempts@extract_filing.py@2026-09-03` (MANUAL_REVIEW, retry_count 10) with the cause overwritten. Two of the six had a recoverable cause from logs: ESDS Software RHP edc03a70, `spawn failed: spawnSync nice ETIMEDOUT` under the then-10-minute EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_MS (log 2026-09-10T18:35:16Z), and an NSE ANCHOR_ALLOCATION_REPORT, `anchor sidecar timed out after 120000ms` (log 2026-09-18T03:18:27Z). The other 4 (PRICE_BAND_AD on swastika-infra, adroit-industries, moneyview; ANCHOR_ALLOCATION_REPORT on shanti-inorganics) had NO recoverable cause: the block marker had overwritten `extraction_error`, the append-only `document_extraction_attempts` table (migration 0065) is not yet applied on staging, and retained logs carried no failure line for them by the time this was read. #396 (same ETIMEDOUT class, prod, 2026-09-07) had been closed by a detector only, per signal-ownership R5 ('fixed on main is not fixed until the signal it closed has gone'), and recurred. Fix: every failure kind still counts toward the 10-attempt limit (no unbounded retry, OD-21/OD-33/section 5.3 'never on a backoff timer'), but the block marker now keeps kind + last cause (`blocked_after_10_attempts kind=<kind> last=<cause> @<version>`). Spec basis: OD-21, OD-33, section 5.3 step 5, section 2.1. Failure classes: `transient-failure-counted-toward-a-permanent-block` and `retry-loop-keeps-only-its-last-cause` (both already registered).

findings.title: two scraper integration test files raced on shared look-alike fixtures under vitest's file-level parallelism, passing alone and failing only when run with the other 51 files in the CI-equivalent invocation
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-26 (#252, PR #1209, closes #252). Running `cd scraper && npx vitest run -c vitest.integration.config.ts` against `ipodhan_test` (the sanctioned tunnel DB) reproduced the CI invocation exactly. `identity-matching-od68.integration.test.ts` and `source-record-keys-od85.integration.test.ts` both PASS when run alone and FAIL when run together with the other 51 integration files (wrong outcome, e.g. `'bound'` vs `'held'`), because they share look-alike fixture rows that vitest's file-level parallelism lets race against each other on the same test database.
