No owning section in `docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md` -- a test-infrastructure defect. Added failure class `shared-fixtures-race-under-file-level-test-parallelism` (status: guarded).

findings.title: With the verdict writer on, witnesses are stored but hold only sources that SUPPLIED a value, and every stored field has exactly one source
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-27 ~11:10 IST, read-only on ipodhan_staging, after ENABLE_VERDICT_WRITER=true was added to the staging scraper env on 2026-09-26 09:56 IST (owner OK; issue #1108 step 1). field_sources rows with witnesses: 0 -> 53 (verdict set on all 53: UNCONFIRMED 52, SINGLE_SOURCE 1; latest 2026-09-27 03:50 UTC). Rows with 2 or more witnesses: 0; IPOs with any: 0. Every sampled witness array holds one DOC entry, e.g. moneyview-ltd (OPEN) ipo_details.freshIssue [{source: DOC, docType: PRICE_BAND_AD, value: 7500000000.00}]. By field: ipos.sector 22, ipo_details.issueType 10, ipo_details.faceValue 7, upiCutoffTime 4, ipos.symbol 3, ipos.issueSize 2. Two causes: (1) CODE -- the walk collects only SUPPLIED answers into witnesses (field-plan-walk.ts S3a, 'every SUPPLIED answer in this pass'), so an abstaining or failing source leaves no trace, while OD-103 requires each answer -- 'a value, an abstention (OD-60), or a failure cause' -- to be stored. (2) COVERAGE -- for these fields the rank 2/3 sources do not answer today (ipo_field_plan reason COVERAGE_GAP 7,857 rows measured 2026-09-25). Staging wake log since the change: 98 error-level lines, none mentioning verdict or witness (Investorgain GMP parse 48, Document BLOCKED_ALL 24, listing source zero rows 6, NSE API 6); not compared against a pre-change window. Consequence: the OD-102 per-source panel would show one value per field and no row for the silent sources. Core proof of issue #1108 step 1: PARTIAL -- writer proven, multi-source not. Spec: §2.4, §9.3, OD-103. Re-measured 2026-09-28 13:1x IST, read-only on ipodhan_staging: witness rows 171 across 87 IPOs, sources CHITTORGARH 120 / DOC 48 / NSE 3, rows with 2+ witnesses still 0. Fields: ipos.listingDate 77, ipos.sector 35, ipo_details.faceValue 14, issueType 11, ipos.issueSize 8 (all fields that were still unsettled). On the 35 live IPOs (OPEN 21, UPCOMING 14) the core reader fields (price_range_min/max, lot_size, open/close_date, issue_size, listing_date) are NOT_AVAILABLE_YET 150 / CHECK_FAILED 48 / SUPPLIED 47, and all 210 have a rank-2 source. Third cause, in code: the NOT_AVAILABLE_YET branch returns after the provisional write and writes no witness, and tryProvisional stops at the first lower-rank SUPPLIED answer. Those 150 rows are re-asked every data slot, so the fix (branch fix/witness-every-answer) fills them without a backfill.

findings.title: The offer document names the listing exchanges and the board in one sentence; it agrees with our stored value on 32 of 33 IPOs and is right on the one disagreement
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-27 on ipodhan_staging, read-only, over document_pages (74 documents with text): 36 IPOs carry the cover-page sentence 'The Equity Shares ... are proposed to be listed on ...' in pages 1-6. In 33 of them a PROSPECTUS (6), RHP (24) or DRHP (3) names the exchanges and the board: main board BSE+NSE 19, main board BSE only 1, SME on NSE Emerge 9, SME on BSE SME 4 (e.g. axiom-gas-engineering-ltd RHP 'SME Platform of National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE EMERGE)'; a-one-steels-india-ltd RHP 'listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange ... findings.title: SEBI's DRHP search page answers a zero-result query with HTTP 200 and a real page, not an error -- a dead or rejected session looks identical unless the marker is read

findings.title: The SEBI listing page is company-independent but was fetched once PER IPO and PER document type, draining the 60-second discovery budget before company-specific document search ran
findings.detail: Root cause measured on a staging cycle, 2026-09-27T20:08Z: networkCalls 200/200 (the request cap), 176 of those 200 to www.sebi.gov.in, found 0 documents. The SEBI listing page 1 and its 6 paged continuations are the same page regardless of which IPO or document type is being searched, but the discovery walk re-fetched them per IPO and per document type -- roughly 8 SEBI requests per IPO. This is the mechanism behind F-151/F-152's "60-second discovery budget runs out each time": a company-independent page consumed the request budget that company-specific search needed. findings.area: pull walk -- admin-held fields skipped, not read
findings.title: The pull walk's per-field loop skips an admin-held field entirely, contrary to §2.4's own clarification that skip means never write, not never read
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-28 on `main`, scraper/src/services/field-plan-walk.ts lines ~691-697: when an admin protection row exists for a field, the walk returns/continues before asking any source -- it does not read the field at all. §2.4's 2026-09-25 clarification (following OD-106, OD-107 and §9.2 item 9) states explicitly: "the 'skip' above means 'never WRITE', not 'never read'. A field an admin holds is still asked at the reads that OD-56 and OD-66 already schedule ... the answer is stored as a witness and, when it differs from the admin value, becomes a suggestion in the admin queue." Consequence: with the code as measured, no witness is ever stored for a held field, so §9.2 item 9 ("a newer document after an admin save" becomes a suggestion) and OD-106 (an E-1 field's newer exchange value alerts the admin) can never fire for any admin-held field -- the admin queue's suggestion mechanism for held fields is silently dead. Fix in progress, branch fix/walk-reads-held-fields.

findings.title: The code's E1_EXCHANGE_STATED_FIELDS constant lists 8 fields plus status; the manifest lists 9 class-T fields including status, and listing_exchanges is class D -- OD-117 states every E-1 field follows OD-106, so the two lists need to agree on what counts
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-28: packages/shared/.../field-sources-repository.ts:90 defines E1_EXCHANGE_STATED_FIELDS as 8 named fields plus status (9 total). Appendix A's manifest independently lists 9 class-T fields including status. findings.area: held-field walk read answered from the admin's own provenance row (§2.4)
findings.title: The held-field walk read could never see a document's value: the DOC fetcher answers a held read from field_sources, which on a held field IS the admin row, so it can only echo the protected value back
findings.detail: F-200 (2026-09-28) found the walk skipped a held field before asking any source; fixed in #1280 (3f1cc6d7, main and staging) -- the walk now reads held fields. This finding (2026-09-29) is the next layer: even after that fix, the DOC fetcher resolves a held read from field_sources, and on a held field field_sources IS the ADMIN row (the admin save writes that row, §9.2 item 3), so the walk's read of a document can never surface a value different from what the admin already holds. Proved red in the item 9 integration test, 2026-09-29. Fix on branch feat/item9-document-suggestions: held reads answer from document_field_receipts (OD-91's best document) instead of field_sources. Failure class held-read-answered-by-own-admin-provenance. Status CARDED: owned by the item 9 build card (docs/design/pull-model-completion-state.md item 9), not yet merged.

findings.area: admin write timestamps vs database-stamped times (§9.2 item 3; consumed by item 9 and item 27)
findings.title: Admin saves stamped their times from the app host clock while the documents and conflicts they are ordered against are stamped by the database clock, so any drift misorders a document against the save
findings.detail: Measured 2026-09-29 by the supervisor: laptop vs database about +0.28 s (an earlier crude measurement said 1.47 s); production app host (Linux VPS) vs laptop about +0.58 s, so app host vs database about 0.3 s today and uncontrolled (nothing keeps them in step). writeAdminFieldValue stamped field_sources.updated_at, field_protection_metadata.manually_edited_at/updated_at and audit_logs.timestamp from new Date() (admin-field-write.ts:696 on main 7ae8c3cf); item 9 (newer-document-suggestions.ts) orders documents.created_at (database defaultNow) against that stamp, and item 27 relaunch-admin-clear.ts orders the same pair; its integration case (d) failed 2 of 3 runs on the laptop. Proved red 2026-09-29 in scraper/tests/integration/admin-write-database-clock.integration.test.ts with the app clock faked 5 min behind (a document first seen BEFORE the save was suggested, 2 suggestions instead of 1) and 5 min ahead (the document first seen AFTER the save was never suggested, 0 instead of 1). Same shape found in field-sources-repository.ts: first INSERT stamped updated_at from new Date(), later UPDATE from now(), so one column mixed two clocks (B1 Tier A review, status ladder guard PR #1260). Fix in PR #1309 (branch fix/admin-write-db-clock): every admin write reads the database clock once per transaction (readDatabaseNow, packages/shared/src/db/database-clock.ts) or stamps sql now(); data_conflicts.detected_at (logConflict, upsertConflict) and resolved_at (autoResolveConverged, resolveConflict, bulkResolveForIPO), ipo_source_keys.state_changed_at and ipos.last_manual_edit_at also stamp sql now() (Tier A review round 2). Proved: with the app clock faked 5 min behind, a conflict's detected_at was 300 s before the database now() before the fix and equals it after. Guarded by scripts/ci/check-app-clock-timestamps.mjs (22 remaining app-clock stamps baselined with reasons: hours-wide freshness bookkeeping, a Redis score, API response metadata). Failure class mixed-clock-ordering.

findings.title: The Notifier's daily digest and every alert timestamp it prints run in the app HOST's local time, not IST, so a host without TZ=Asia/Kolkata silently moves the promised 09:00 IST digest and mislabels every alert time
findings.detail: Read 2026-09-29 23:45 IST: `/root/notifier/src/digest.ts:71` compares `now.getHours()` against the configured daily time `"09:00"` (`config.ts:139`) using the process's local hour, and `src/format.ts:17-20` prints alert times with `getHours()`/`getMinutes()`, both local. The box's system TZ is `Asia/Kolkata`, but the notifier's pm2 process env carried no `TZ` variable (read 2026-09-29 23:45 IST) — so today the local hour happens to equal IST only because the OS default matches; nothing pins it. Setting `TZ=UTC` on that pm2 process (a plausible "make it explicit" fix) would move the 09:00 IST digest to fire at 14:30 IST and print every alert time in UTC on an India-only alert channel (OD-112, §9.2 item 16: "the 09:00 IST digest"). Open for owner decision (Q-C3-2): pin `TZ=Asia/Kolkata` explicitly on the notifier's pm2 env (belt-and-braces over the current OS-default reliance) so a future host move or pm2 env reset cannot silently shift the digest.

findings.title: NSE and BSE together serve only 2 of the 6 E-1 timetable fields OD-106/OD-141 promise an exchange release for; the other 4 can never be released by an exchange the way the spec describes
findings.detail: `NSE_SERVEABLE_FIELDS` (`scraper/src/services/field-plan-walk-nse-fetcher.ts:48`, confirmed via its only import at `field-plan-walk-deps.ts:78,256`) serves `openDate`/`closeDate` only; every other E-1 date the NSE fetcher is asked for (listing, allotment, basis, refund, credit) answers `CHECK_FAILED`. The BSE fetcher (`scraper/src/scrapers/field-plan-walk-bse-fetcher.ts`) serves `issueSize` only among the fields this class covers — no grep hit for `CHECK_FAILED` inside it returning any E-1 date. So an OD-106/OD-141 exchange-release event, as coded today, can only ever fire for `open_date`/`close_date`; the four other E-1 fields (listing, allotment, basis-of-allotment, refund/credit dates) have no exchange source able to release an admin value the way §9.2 item 28 describes, and any admin correction on those four is effectively permanent until an admin clears it. Open for owner decision (Q-C3-3): either narrow OD-106/OD-141's promise to the two exchange-serveable fields, or name the source (a document re-read trigger) that is meant to release the other four.

findings.area: market_holidays reference data (exchange holiday calendar; working_days_inclusive; OD-21 listing_t3/listing_t6; scheduler calendar gates)
findings.title: The 23 NSE-only 2025 trading-holiday rows are each stored one day early (an IST date shifted through UTC); they are the only NSE-vs-BSE difference in the table
findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-02 00:3x IST on ipodhan_staging, read-only via docs/design/probes/market-holidays.mjs (_lib.mjs openReadOnlyPool). market_holidays holds 2024 BOTH/TRADING 18 rows, 2025 BOTH/TRADING 20, 2025 NSE/TRADING 23, 2026 BOTH/TRADING 20; no BSE-only rows. Every 2025 NSE-only row is the same holiday as a BOTH row one calendar day earlier: Holi NSE 2025-03-13 (Thu) vs BOTH 2025-03-14; Good Friday NSE 2025-04-17 (a Thursday) vs BOTH 2025-04-18; Independence Day 2025-08-14 vs 2025-08-15; Christmas 2025-12-24 vs 2025-12-25; Mahashivratri 2025-02-25 vs 2025-02-26. Trading-holiday dates present for NSE and absent for BSE: 21 (13 on weekdays); BSE-only: 0. So the NSE and BSE calendars are the SAME set and the apparent difference is the shift defect (the mechanism is the IST-to-UTC date shift of .claude/rules/ist-timezone.md; the writer of these rows is not yet identified). 2024 and 2026 rows match known dates where checked (2024 Good Friday 03-29, Holi 03-25; 2026 Good Friday 04-03, Republic Day 01-26); 2026 completeness against the official NSE list is unverified. Two same-date pairs are real double holidays (2025-10-02 Gandhi Jayanti + Dussehra; 2026-05-01 Maharashtra Day + Buddha Purnima), not duplicates. Impact: with NSE rows included, 13 real 2025 trading days count as holidays, so a working-day rule (listing_t3/listing_t6, #1380) judging a 2025 listing counts too few working days and accepts a late listing; the scheduler calendar gates read the same table (due-step-cycle.ts, document-cycle-calendar-gate.ts, live-slot-miss-monitor.ts) but only for current dates, so 2026 scheduling is not affected. Open: repair (retire the 23 shifted rows; staging after a dry run, prod on the owner's word) and a detection check (an exchange-specific trading holiday on a weekday that the other exchange does not share).

findings.area: NSE holiday-master API (source of the exchange holiday calendar, F-220/F-221)
findings.title: NSE's holiday API publishes only the current year, and the old writer read the corporate-bonds segment (CBM) instead of equity (CM)
findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-02 by the PR #1448 builder: one live call (homepage cookie visit, then https://www.nseindia.com/api/holiday-master?type=trading) returned HTTP 200, 34,022 bytes, saved unchanged as scraper/tests/fixtures/nse/holiday-master-trading-2026-10-02.json. The CM (equity) list for 2026 has 20 dates, 16 on weekdays: the 15 broker-published dates of F-221 plus 2026-01-15 (Maharashtra municipal-election closure), which the broker lists omitted. The response carries no 2025 rows, so NSE's API cannot repair the 23 shifted 2025 rows of F-220 (PR #1444's repair-shifted-market-holidays.ts covers those) and cannot seed a past year. web/lib/scrapers/sources/market-holidays-scraper.ts read segment CBM (corporate bonds), not CM; the two lists are identical today, so the wrong segment produced correct dates by coincidence. Implication: a year's calendar must be reconciled from NSE while that year is current; a past year can only be checked against a saved NSE answer.

findings.title: Keyed child-table provenance rows carry no document lineage; only the table's IPO-level `rows` record names the document
findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-02 on ipodhan_staging (read-only, docs/design/probes/_lib.mjs openReadOnlyPool): field_sources rows with source DRHP, row_key <> '' on child tables: 11,020, of which 11,020 have data_lineage docType NULL and documentId NULL (updated_by SYSTEM only). findings.area: §2.5.6 item 2; DOC label (PRICE_BAND_AD); extractor advert patterns
findings.title: A price-band advert regex let an optional currency-glyph slot swallow the band's leading digit, so 172-182 was stored as 72-82
findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-03 on ipodhan_staging (read-only): glass-wall-systems-india-ltd stores price_range_min/max 72/82, field_sources source DRHP (label DOC), from PRICE_BAND_AD extracted by extract_filing.py at 2026-09-27; lot_size 82 comes from BSE. The real band is Rs 172-182, lot 82, issue Rs 427.89 crore (https://choiceindia.com/news/glass-wall-systems-india-ipo-subscription-day-2 ; https://www.indiainfoline.com/news/companies/glass-wall-systems-ipo-gmp-price-band-dates-allotment-financials-and-key-details ; https://www.kotakneo.com/news/ipos/glass-wall-systems-shares-list-at-a-7-percent-premium/). The leading '1' was dropped, so a value 100 below the real one was stored. CAUSE (proven 2026-10-03, PR #1483): not OCR digit loss; the advert's price-band and face-value patterns allowed any one character before the number to stand for the rupee sign, and when the sign was absent that slot consumed the first digit ("172.00 TO 182.00" read 72/82; face value 10 read 0). Over all 76 stored staging adverts, 18 read differently once the slot excludes digits; 16 of those had been refused. Class: docs/reviews/failure-classes/optional-glyph-slot-swallows-a-leading-digit.json (#1483). Discriminating measure: lot_size x price_range_max outside Rs 13,000-16,000 on MAINBOARD IPO-type rows with open_date >= 2024-01-01 flags 7 of 110 rows on staging. glass-wall-systems-india-ltd is the only DOC-sourced one and the only one confirmed wrong. The other 6 are unverified: kwality-walls-india-ltd 21-21 lot 100 (BSE); pngs-reva-diamond-jewellery-ltd 386-386 lot 32 (CHITTORGARH); om-power-transmission-ltd 175-175 lot 100 (CHITTORGARH); suryo-foods-industries-ltd 15-15 lot 3000 (no source row); icici-prudential-asset-management-company 2061-2165 lot 100 (CHITTORGARH); stallion-india-fluorochemicals-ltd 85-90 lot 4000 (CHITTORGARH). Open for owner decision on the check threshold. Issue #1477.

findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-03 01:28 IST, read-only, one NSE session: RUNWALENTR (Runwal Enterprises, CLOSED 29-Sep-2026) is absent from /api/ipo-current-issue (VNL, NITYAS, EVENTIONS) and /api/all-upcoming-issues (VNL, NITYAS, SMCG04, RKFAL), while /api/ipo-detail?symbol=RUNWALENTR still serves issueInfo.dataList with 'Price Range' = 'Rs. 290 to Rs. 305 per Equity Share', 'Issue Period' 25-Sep-2026 to 29-Sep-2026, 'Bid Lot' 49 (fixtures scraper/tests/fixtures/nse/*.live-2026-10-03.json). The walk's NSE fetcher read only the boards, so every later NSE ask for an off-board IPO answered NOT_AVAILABLE_YET or, when the board scrape failed, CHECK_FAILED 'NSE board empty'. findings.area: §2.5.6 item 5; Appendix A rows 56-81 (financial_data); OD-99 writer capability; item 43
findings.title: The field-plan walk cannot write financial_data: an IPO-level answer is refused MISSING_ROW_KEY, so a website value never reaches the page
findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-03 from code on main 557e368e8 (item 43 round 2): financial_data is one row per IPO (schema.ts financialData.ipoId unique), but it is in neither SINGLETON_ROW_CHILD_TABLES (consolidated-writer-capability.ts: ipo_details, anchor_investors) nor CHILD_ROW_TABLES (packages/shared child-row-field-writer.ts). A walk write for (financial_data, row_key '') is refused by data-consolidation-orchestrator.ts (rowKey === '' on a non-singleton table -> MISSING_ROW_KEY, a structural skip parked WRITER_CANNOT_ACCEPT), and DOC_READABLE_TABLES is [ipos, ipo_details], so DOC does not answer it either. Effect: the 21 Chittorgarh financial_data pairs mapped in item 43 round 2 (e.g. Runwal Enterprises net_worth 768.20, market_cap 4507.61, promoter holding 95.16 / 84.6) are read and recorded as answers but are not written; the staging NSE field table of 2026-10-02 lists 20 financial_data columns empty. The rule is settled by the spec: OD-73 (the published value is the highest-ranked SUPPLIED answer) with Appendix A ranks (DOC above CHITTORGARH for every one of these fields) means a Chittorgarh answer may fill an EMPTY financial_data field or be recorded as a witness, and never replaces a DOC-supplied value. The remaining gap is technical only: the walk writer has no row key for financial_data (add it as a one-row-per-IPO table honouring OD-73), not a decision.

findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-03 on live Chittorgarh detail pages: the valuation table prints 'Market Cap at Offer Price' with a Pre IPO and a Post IPO cell (Runwal Enterprises 4,007.44 Cr / 4,507.61 Cr; Vishal Nirmiti 435.60 / 580.60; Dove Soft 211.55 / 270.69). extractFinancialsFromDetailHtml (chittorgarh-detail-fields.ts, used only by the backfill script) reads the Pre IPO cell, while Appendix A row 72 says market_cap = post-issue shares x cap. findings.title: NSE ipo-detail replies for SME issues carry no company name, so the walk's identity check refuses every SME ipo-detail read
findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-03 on live ipo-detail replies (fixtures ipo-detail-EVENTIONS / GREENASIA .live-2026-10-03.json, both series=SME): issueInfo.dataList[0].title is null (the first row is the SEBI-circular note), top-level companyName is the SYMBOL ('EVENTIONS', 'GREENASIA') and metaInfo is {}. Mainboard replies (RUNWALENTR, MONEYVIEW) carry the company name as dataList[0].title and metaInfo.companyName. parseNseDetailFields requires the name to match (PR #1488 review), so for every SME IPO each NSE ipo-detail answer (the #1486 off-board fallback and the item 43 detail-only fields) is CHECK_FAILED 'detail identity unproven'. Open for owner decision: whether an exact symbol match on the IPO's own ACTIVE NSE_ISSUE key (OD-85) with series SME proves identity for SME replies. DECIDED 2026-10-03 as OD-170 (decision D3) (owner delegated night decisions to supervisor + reviewer; PR #1497): an SME reply without a name proves identity ONLY when (a) the key's series is SME, dataList[0].title is null and companyName equals the symbol (a reply carrying any other name is still refused), (b) the symbol asked is the IPO's ACTIVE NSE_ISSUE key, and (c) the stated open AND close dates (the 'Revised/Extended Issue Period' row when printed, F-237) equal the stored ipos.open_date and close_date, both present; anything else is CHECK_FAILED 'detail identity unproven'. Side effect, fails closed: a relaunched SME issue with new dates (OD-83) reads CHECK_FAILED until the board path updates the stored dates.

findings.title: NSE prints an extended issue's dates under 'Revised/Extended Issue Period ' (trailing space), which the ipo-detail period reader does not read
findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-03 on the live GREENASIA (SME, listed) ipo-detail reply: no 'Issue Period' row; instead 'Revised/Extended Issue Period ' = '"24-Sep-2026 to 01-Oct-2026 (The Issue is further extended from start date 24-09-2026 to end date 01-10-2026)"', and 'Revised Cut-off time for UPI Mandate Confirmation' in place of the original cut-off row. The item 43 UPI cut-off reader reads the Revised row first; the open/close-date reader (#1486) reads only 'Issue Period', so an extended issue's dates abstain from ipo-detail. Unmeasured: how many stored IPOs had an extended period. Since OD-170 (PR #1497) both the SME identity check and the open/close-date field readers read the Revised row when printed.

findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-03: EVENTIONS and GREENASIA print '10.00 a.m. to 5.00 p.m. (Bidding Timings on Issue Closure upto 4:00 P.M.)' findings.title: A document record newer than a plan row's last attempt re-opened nothing: capped or gap-stamped DOC-ranked rows never asked DOC again
findings.detail: Measured read-only on ipodhan_staging 2026-10-03 06:40 IST: 232 DOC rank-1 plan rows (row_key '') not SUPPLIED held a document_field_receipts value newer than last_attempt_at, on 52 IPOs. Blockers by the claim legs: CHECK_FAILED at attempts >= FIELD_PLAN_RECLAIM_MAX_ATTEMPTS 77 (e.g. nityas-gems-and-jewellery-ltd price_range_min/max and lot_size at 16 attempts, record 70/75/200 from 2026-10-03 00:47 UTC, stored 70/75/200); CHECK_FAILED gap-stamped with a key the re-read under the same extractor version did not change 123 (e.g. nityas ipos.objectives, stamped @2026-10-04 at 23:12 UTC, record at 00:18 UTC); held-read 1 (by design); LISTED rows outside the live window waiting for the closed-IPO job 31. 154 rows sit on IPOs in the document cycle's live window, 78 outside. Fixed by the receipt_newer claim leg (OD-171): the real listReceiptNewerRows on staging selects 243 rows / 52 IPOs (214 CHECK_FAILED, 28 NOT_AVAILABLE_YET, 1 PENDING), nityas 5 (cin, lot_size, objectives, price_range_min, price_range_max; segment excluded as held).

findings.title: The DOC fetcher has no answer for an EMPTY column with no provenance row even when a document record holds the value
findings.detail: Measured read-only on ipodhan_staging 2026-10-03: of the 232 F-239 rows, 18 are ipos fields with no field_sources row (e.g. nityas-gems-and-jewellery-ltd ipos.objectives NULL while its RHP record holds [{amount:70, Funding Working Capital ...}]). The fetcher's own-record path (OD-161) serves only website-owned columns and the DRHP path needs DRHP provenance, so a re-opened row is answered CHECK_FAILED NO_DOCUMENT_PROVENANCE again: re-asked once, still unanswered, no loop. Owners of the other rows: DRHP 133, BSE 37, CHITTORGARH 40, NSE 3, ADMIN 1. Settled by OD-161 ("the DOC fetcher reads a document's answer from its own record, never from who owns the stored value"; supervisor ruling 2026-10-03, not an owner decision). FIXED (fix/doc-receipt-empty-column, refs #1500): an empty column with no provenance row is answered from the best in-family COMPLETED document's own receipt, decoded to the column shape from the schema; TEXT or unknown mark writes through the walk (which records the field_sources row), OCR/MIXED is kept empty and listed for the admin, two receipts the OD-91 comparator cannot order fail closed. Re-measured read-only on ipodhan_staging 2026-10-03 03:30 UTC (docs/design/probes/f240-doc-receipt-empty-column.mts): 27 ipos rows on 26 IPOs, before 27 CHECK_FAILED NO_DOCUMENT_PROVENANCE, after 20 SUPPLIED (nityas objectives from its RHP) and 7 companyDescription rows whose only receipt is outside the field's RHP family (OD-96, unchanged).
